case_title: Sher Singh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
accused_occupation: Teacher (as stated in counsel's submission for one accused)
accused_victim_relationship: Land rival / prior dispute: dispute between the victim and an accused over sale of land
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149; IPC s.323 r/w s.149; IPC s.148
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured wife and son), medical (post-mortem), circumstantial (site plans), recovery of articles
confession: None (no confession; a kulhari was recovered on interrogation of one accused, not relied on as a confession)
aggravating_circumstances: Multiple accused armed with weapons; 26 injuries including fractures, rib fractures lacerating the liver, injuries on vital parts; injuries to wife and son
mitigating_circumstances: None noted (High Court's reliance on injuries to non-vital parts was rejected by the Supreme Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of s.302/149, 323/149, 148 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs.300 each; 2 months RI (s.323/149) and 1 year RI (s.148), concurrent; two co-accused acquitted
high_court_outcome: Conviction altered from s.302/149 to s.304 Part II/149 IPC; 5 years RI and fine Rs.50,000 each; other sentences maintained
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 r/w s.149 (murder); s.323 r/w s.149; s.148 IPC
neutral_facts: On the morning of 29 September 1991, the victim went to his field to harvest a bajra crop with his wife and son. A group of persons arrived armed with an axe, sickles, sticks and a jailli. They raised a challenge that they would teach the victim a lesson for interfering in a land purchase. One attacker struck the victim's knee with an axe, others felled him and beat him with sticks and sickles, and the attackers also struck the victim's wife and son when they tried to intervene. A bystander who intervened was struck on the knee. Attracted by an alarm, other villagers arrived. The attackers then lifted the injured victim and carried him to a tubewell belonging to one of the group, where he was left bleeding, and the attackers ran away. The victim's son informed the village, and the injured were taken to a Primary Health Centre. The victim was referred to a civil hospital, where he died the same afternoon. The victim's wife and son were discharged after medical examination. The wife's statement was recorded in the evening and a first information report was registered that night. The post-mortem report recorded 26 injuries, including fractures of both forearm bones, both leg bones and a foot, fractures of the ninth and tenth right ribs that lacerated the liver, and the doctor opined that the injuries were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. Investigating officers visited the field and the tubewell, collected chappals, a broken rapri, a rope, a blood-stained matchbox and blood-stained earth, and prepared site plans which matched the revenue official's plan. A kulhari was recovered on the interrogation of one of the accused. The defence stated that a defence witness had been injured in the same incident, but the X-ray film of that witness was not traceable and the injuries were not shown to be connected with the incident.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; 26 injuries including fractures of both forearm bones, both leg bones and a foot, and fractures of the 9th and 10th right ribs lacerating the liver; injuries to the victim's wife and son
premeditation_planning: Not identified: the court did not find premeditation or planning; it found the intention to cause death was evident from the injuries
motive: alleged: the victim had interfered in the purchase of agricultural land (dispute over land sale)
key_evidence_accepted: Ocular testimony of the injured wife and son (PW-1, PW-6), admitted to be present by the defence; post-mortem report and doctor's opinion; site plans and recoveries
witness_credibility: Injured eyewitnesses' presence admitted by the defence; delay in recording the wife's statement held explicable and not held against the prosecution; defence alibi witnesses found unreliable
post_offence_conduct: Left the injured victim at the tubewell and fled the spot
bail_history: On bail at the High Court stage; High Court directed custody to undergo the remaining sentence
trial_duration: offence: 29.9.1991; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 01.10.2008; Supreme Court: 16.12.2010
legal_representation: Accused: R.S. Cheema (Crl.A. 1071/2009) and K.B. Sinha (Crl.A. 1294/2009); counsel for the State and the complainant not individually named
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge-sheet filed against the main accused and others; further accused summoned under s.319 CrPC; investigation completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted as a lapse by the court; FIR delay held insignificant; delay in the defence witness's X-ray examination noted, with the film not traceable
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302/149 (life imprisonment). High Court: s.302/149 conviction set aside, convicted under s.304 Part II/149 with 5 years RI. Supreme Court: High Court judgment set aside and trial court judgment restored
prosecution_argument: Incident occurred in the victim's field and he was carried to the tubewell (site plans and recoveries support this); no delay in FIR; no obligation to explain the defence witness's injuries; alibi not cogent; High Court wrongly applied s.304 Part II instead of murder
defence_argument: FIR delayed and used to fabricate the story and shift the site of incident; injuries on the defence witness suppressed; no close relationship between the families; alibi established; reliance on Babu Ram, Binay Kumar Singh and Jayantibhai
legal_principle_applied: Intention to cause death inferred from the number, nature and location of injuries and medical opinion on sufficiency in ordinary course of nature; delay in FIR and non-explanation of unconnected injuries not fatal to prosecution; alibi must create a real doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Binay Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (1996) 8 Suppl. SCR 225 = (1997) 1 SCC 283 (held inapplicable); Jayantibhai Bhenkarbhai v. State of Gujarat (2002) 2 Suppl. SCR 255 = (2002) 8 SCC 165 (held inapplicable); Babu Ram & Ors. v. State of Punjab (2008) 3 SCC 709 (held inapplicable)
sentencing_rationale: Injuries and medical opinion showed intention to cause death, so the offence was not reduced to s.304 Part II; trial court's life imprisonment restored
judicial_aggravating_factors: Large number of injuries including fractures and injuries on vital parts; rib fractures damaging abdominal and thoracic organs; multiple armed attackers
